title: Sum of the reply: no circle, no infinite regress — Scripture known by implanted signs
source_text: XXXIV. Huc ergo redit summa responsionis nostrae, in fidei analysi nec dari posse circulum, nec progressum in infinitum, sed mentem nostram necessario sisti in aliquo Dei verbo quod per aliud Dei verbum non confirmetur, sed quod fides nostra suscipiat immediate & propter se, & in cujus notitiam & fidem adducamur per argumenta & signa insita, aliaque, ut loquuntur scholae, credendi motiva, non ex testimonio alterius cujusdam verbi divini desumpta. Istud autem Dei verbum, in quo sistitur fides nostra, esse Scripturam sacram, constantem certo numero librorum θεοπνεύστων, ac proinde illam a nobis non suscipi propter aliquod aliud Dei verbum quod testimonium illi perhibeat, nec etiam illam se nobis probare simplici & nudo suo testimonio, sed nobis innotescere ex signis & notis insitis aliisque argumentis atque incitamentis. Inde vero minime sequi illam non esse perfectam & sufficientem fidei regulam: quoniam in tali regula non requiritur ut aliter se probet, sed satis est ut, illa excepta, omnia quae ad fidem pertinent possint testimonio illius confirmari. Imo impossibile est dari talem regulam fidei, quae seipsam, sicut caetera, possit simplici suo testimonio probare: prorsus vero necessarium primam fidei regulam inter Christianos tanquam principium supponi, nec per alia fidei principia probari, nisi forte ad hominem, & a posteriori, ut loquuntur in scholis.
pass_a_gloss: To this therefore returns the sum of our response, that in the analysis of faith neither a circle can be given, nor a progress to infinity, but our mind must necessarily be stopped in some word of God which is not confirmed by another word of God, but which our faith receives immediately and for its own sake, and into whose knowledge and faith we are led by arguments and implanted signs, and other motives of believing, as the schools speak, not taken from the testimony of some other divine word. But that that word of God, in which our faith is stopped, is sacred Scripture, consisting of a certain number of God-breathed books, and accordingly that it is not received by us on account of some other word of God which bears testimony to it, nor indeed that it proves itself to us by its simple and naked testimony, but becomes known to us from implanted signs and notes and other arguments and incentives. And thence it by no means follows that it is not a perfect and sufficient rule of faith: because in such a rule it is not required that it prove itself otherwise, but it is enough that, it excepted, all things which pertain to faith can be confirmed by its testimony. Nay it is impossible that such a rule of faith be given which can prove itself, like the rest, by its simple testimony: but it is altogether necessary that the first rule of faith among Christians be supposed as a principle, and not be proved by other principles of faith, except perhaps ad hominem, and a posteriori, as they speak in the schools.
pass_b_english: Faith-analysis allows neither a circle nor infinite regress — the mind must stop in a word received immediately for itself.
That word is sacred Scripture (a fixed number of God-breathed books), known by implanted signs, not by another divine word's bare certificate.
Self-knowledge by innate notes does not strip Scripture's perfection as faith-rule.
A rule need not prove itself the way it proves everything else — first principles are supposed, proved at most ad hominem / a posteriori.
